bug_description.normalized: net-snmp accepts an `oldEngineID` configuration value and records its parsed octet-string length in `oldEngineIDLength` without enforcing that the value is at least 4 bytes long. Later, `setup_engineID` reuses that stored length as the size of a fresh heap buffer for a new engine ID and then unconditionally copies a 4-byte enterprise identifier into the buffer. The saved ASAN trace shows the crashing run allocated only a 1-byte destination at `calloc(1, len)` and immediately performed a `WRITE of size 4` in `setup_engineID`, producing the heap-buffer-overflow.

source.description: First project-code statement that consumes the attacker-selected `oldEngineID` argument value and materializes vulnerability-relevant state for the later engine-ID setup path.
source.value_from: The staged PoC bytes contain the argv token `--oldEngineID`. Project code registers that keyword with `oldengineID_conf`, and this statement parses the following value string into `oldEngineID` plus `oldEngineIDLength`, which `setup_engineID` later trusts as an allocation size.

sink.description: ASAN crash site. `setup_engineID` writes the fixed 4-byte Net-SNMP enterprise identifier into the heap buffer sized from `len`; the saved sanitizer trace shows that allocation was only 1 byte in the crashing execution.

root_cause.description: `oldengineID_conf` stores whatever parsed octet-string length the config parser returns and performs no minimum-size validation before later code reuses that length as the destination size for a buffer that must first hold a 4-byte enterprise prefix.

tainted_value_origin.description: For a hex-form octet string, the config parser derives a byte count `ilen`, allocates `ilen + 1` bytes, copies `ilen` bytes of parsed data, and stores that byte count in `*len`. This is the source of the attacker-controlled length later propagated as `oldEngineIDLength`.

parser_admitted.description: Sample-specific dispatch gate. The config/parser path reaches the vulnerable state update only when the keyword resolves to the registered `oldEngineID` handler.

coarse_trace.summary: Argument parsing hands control to `init_snmp`, which reads configuration and can dispatch the attacker-selected `oldEngineID` keyword to the SNMPv3 config handler.
The `oldEngineID` handler parses the supplied octet string into `oldEngineID` and records its length in `oldEngineIDLength` without a minimum-size check.
During post-config initialization, the library invokes `setup_engineID(NULL, NULL)` when no explicit engine ID has already been set.
`setup_engineID` reuses `oldEngineIDLength` as the heap allocation size and then copies a fixed 4-byte enterprise identifier into that buffer, causing the overflow reported by ASAN.

fine_trace.note: The `oldEngineID` config value is parsed into a heap-backed byte string and a recorded byte length, and that state is stored globally for later SNMPv3 engine-ID setup.

For hex-form input, the parser derives a byte count `ilen` from the token text, allocates `ilen + 1` bytes for the parsed buffer, and stores `ilen` in `*len`, so the saved length directly reflects the attacker-controlled octet-string size.

`oldengineID_conf` accepts the parsed `oldEngineIDLength` as-is and stores it for later use; there is no source-side check that this length is at least the 4 bytes needed for the enterprise prefix copied in `setup_engineID`.
After configuration has been read, the post-config callback reaches the vulnerable builder on the path where no explicit engine ID was already set.
On the `oldEngineID`-present path inside the NETSNMP_RND engine-ID builder, `setup_engineID` replaces the default computed length with the previously stored `oldEngineIDLength`.
The reused `len` value becomes the destination heap-buffer size. In the saved crashing run, ASAN reports this allocation produced a 1-byte region.

Before any later copy of `oldEngineID` bytes, the NETSNMP_RND path unconditionally writes the fixed 4-byte Net-SNMP enterprise identifier into `bufp`. With the 1-byte allocation reported by ASAN, this `WRITE of size 4` overruns the heap buffer and is the observed sink.

sanitizer_ground_truth.source: Stage 01 reproduction_report.json, sanitizer_trace.txt, and the staged vulnerable source.

poc.trigger: Run the staged `snmp_parse_args_fuzzer` on the saved PoC so project argument/config parsing routes the `--oldEngineID` input into `oldengineID_conf`, then `init_snmp` reaches the post-config callback that calls `setup_engineID(NULL, NULL)`.

format.name: net-snmp command-line/config argument stream
format.contract: The staged PoC must contain the `--oldEngineID` option and a following value that the project parser accepts as an octet string short enough that `setup_engineID` later allocates too small a destination. The saved ASAN evidence narrows the witnessed crash to the case where `calloc(1, len)` produced a 1-byte buffer before the fixed 4-byte `memcpy` into that buffer.
